title: We Participate. God Transforms.
headline: Can You Change Yourself? Effort, Grace and the Spirit
tagline: Transformation requires our participation, but it never becomes our self-creation.
seo_title: Can You Change Yourself? Effort, Grace and the Holy Spirit | TheWrkShop
seo_description: You can produce discipline, but not the fruit of the Spirit. A devotional for men on 2 Corinthians 3:18, Galatians 5:16 and John 15:5.
verse_text: And we all…. are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

scriptures.text: And we all…. are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
I am the vine; you are the branches….apart from me you can do nothing.

items: We have spent many days talking about things you can do.
Recognize.
Capture.
Test.
Surrender.
Replace.
Obey.
Return.
Remain.
Behold.
After enough days of verbs, something dangerous can quietly happen.
You can begin believing transformation depends entirely on you.
If I can just become disciplined enough.
Self-aware enough.
Consistent enough.
If I can master the framework, I can rebuild myself.
Christianity says no.
You participate.
But you are not your own creator.
2 Corinthians 3:18 says “are being transformed.”
Not “transform yourselves.”
Someone else is acting.
“….which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.”

blocks.text: We behold. The Spirit transforms. We become.
“If I try hard enough, I can produce Christlikeness.”

items: You can produce discipline.
You can change routines and environments.
You can memorize Scripture and develop habits.
All of those can matter enormously.
But Galatians doesn’t call love, joy, peace and self-control the fruit of human optimization.
It calls them the fruit of the Spirit.
That keeps us from two errors.
One says, “God transforms me, therefore I do nothing.”
The other says, “Transformation requires effort, therefore everything depends on me.”
Dependence does not eliminate participation. Participation does not eliminate dependence.
The branch does not manufacture life. It remains connected to the Vine.
Grace does not eliminate training. Grace changes why and how we train.
Effort is not the same as earning.
Participate fully. Depend completely.
